html:
The Bechuanaland Protectorate was the British protectorate over the Tswana states of what is now Botswana, declared in 1885 and lasting until independence in 1966.

Britain wanted to keep the road north from the Cape to the interior out of Boer and German hands. It spent almost nothing on the territory and governed it from Mafeking, a town outside its borders in South Africa. The chiefs kept wide power, and cattle and labour on South African mines were the economy.

Like Basutoland, it was kept out of the Union of South Africa in 1910, against South African pressure. At independence in 1966 it had only a few kilometres of paved road. The chiefs' stand in 1895, led by Khama III, had saved it from Rhodes, and Gaborone was built as its new capital.
sum: The Bechuanaland Protectorate was the British protectorate over the Tswana states of what is now Botswana, declared in 1885 and lasting until independence in 1966.
